handoff:

- What: Added a headless, repeatable 2-instance network smoke test that launches one host + one client Godot process on localhost via NetworkManager.host()/join(), and asserts from their logs that the connection succeeded (automated proof for the Exit Gate item 'two instances connect + log confirms peer joined'). Only new files added; NetworkManager.gd/project.godot/MainMenu.gd untouched.
- Files: tests/net/net_smoke_peer.gd (standalone SceneTree `-s` entrypoint, role via --role=host|client), tests/net/run_net_smoke.sh (bash driver; GODOT_BIN env override, ubuntu-CI compatible)
- How to test (2 machines / 2 instances, manual GUI equivalent): Machine/Window A: MainMenu -> Host (port 7777). Machine/Window B: MainMenu -> Join 127.0.0.1:7777 (or A's LAN IP). Expect A's console: `[NET] peer joined: <id>`; B's console: `[NET] connection succeeded (client connected to host)`. Automated equivalent: `GODOT_BIN="C:/Tools/Godot/Godot_v4.7-stable_win64_console.exe" bash tests/net/run_net_smoke.sh` -> prints both logs + `NET SMOKE: PASS`. - Risks/limits: Automated test proves localhost (2 processes, 1 machine) connectivity only; true 2-machine LAN test is still a human/QA follow-up per the card's note. Client-side has a fixed 1.5s post-connect grace period before quitting (found during testing: the client's own connection_succeeded fires before the host finishes its side of the handshake; quitting instantly tore down the socket before the host's peer_connected packet was received/processed) -- bounded and deterministic, not a flaky sleep. Not wired into CI (see report recommendation to producer/tools-devops). Logs are written to the OS temp dir, gitignored, never into the repo tree.

title: ทำ Tag detection: Area3D รอบเสือ ตรวจผู้เล่นที่เข้าใกล้
parked: AUTOMATION GATE GREEN, HUMAN 2-INSTANCE PENDING (2026-07-13). Host-authoritative Area3D proximity sensor as a plain Player-root component (TagDetectorComponent.gd + pure TagRules.gd), role-agnostic, RPC-free; feeds TK-P2-03. code-review APPROVE-WITH-NITS (no S0/S1/S2). architect APPROVED placement (sensor != ability; binding invariant: TagDetector stays RPC-free) — Ability_System_Design.md §2/§3/§4b + Change Log [0.39] amended. qa PASS own run: import clean, GUT 201/201 (+17 TagRules), net_smoke + spawn_probe + spawn_probe_together PASS (no Player.tscn spawn regression). RESUME = human 2-instance check (needs temp debug prints in _on_body_entered/_exited): (1) two players within 2m -> body_entered fires + tag_target_in_range(tagger,target) with correct peer ids; (2) HOST-ONLY EMIT holds (fires server=true on host, NOT on client); (3) leave range -> tag_target_left_range + get_candidates_in_range() empties; (4) despawn a peer in range -> no stale candidate, no crash on body.name (document whether left_range fires -> TK-P2-03 poll-vs-event); (5) floor not a candidate. title: ทำ Tag Sequence (state machine ย่อย): 1) เสือจับล็อกผู้เล่น 2) ทุ่มลงพื้น 3) เล่นเอฟเฟกต์กลายร่าง 4) ผู้เล่นที่ถูกทุ่มกลายเป็นเสือใหม่ 5) เสือเดิมกลับเป็นคน 6) เสือเดิมย้ายออกนอก Safe Circle 7) กลับสู่สถานะ Playing

title: สร้าง Role state machine (Outer / Tiger) และสลับ property/กล้องเมื่อจบ Tag Sequence
notes: STARTED 2026-07-14 (TK-P2-03 human 2-instance PASS 5/5, unblocked). SCOPE FLAG before implementing: this card's title includes '...สลับ property/กล้อง' (swap property/camera) but TK-P2-05 ('สลับกล้อง First Person เสือ/Third Person ตามบทบาท') is a SEPARATE card that depends_on this one and owns the actual FP/TP camera swap -- do not build FP camera here, just confirm/flag the boundary (this card = role property/state + whatever camera-relevant state TK-P2-05 will need e.g. an is_tiger/role signal; TK-P2-05 = the actual view swap). Also: TK-P2-03 already landed real groundwork that may cover most of this card's SM surface -- Player.gd:245 set_role(new_role) already sets `role` and propagates to ability_controller.set_role() (Tiger/Outer ability catalog swap), and GameManager.apply_role_switch() already RPCs both role flips at Tag Sequence step 4+5. Gameplay-engineer: if investigation shows this card is substantially already done by that existing code, DO NOT close silently -- report back with what's missing (if anything: e.g. explicit state validation/guard against invalid transitions, unit tests for the SM in isolation, RoundManager-facing property swap beyond ability catalog) and propose a re-scope for producer/architect sign-off before flipping to done. CAMERA ITSELF CONFIRMED OUT OF SCOPE: did not touch CameraComponent.gd at all -- TK-P2-05 owns the actual FP/TP view swap per its own card + design doc §5 step 3, this card only leaves the signal hook. TESTS ADDED: tests/test_role_state_machine.gd (16 cases) -- RoleRules.is_valid_role() pure cases, MovementComponent.speed_profile_multiplier() pure cases (incl. zero-walk div-by-zero guard), MovementComponent.set_role() bare-instance cases (no scene tree needed, mirrors test_tag_sequence.gd's bare TagAbility pattern), and full Player.tscn integration cases (spawn defaults to Outer profile, set_role(tiger) distributes to both MovementComponent + AbilityController, role_changed signal fires with the new role, an invalid role is rejected + does not emit the signal, idempotent re-apply). Full regression re-run clean: GUT 238/238 (1378 asserts), no S0/S1. SIDE FINDING (fixed test-locally, flagged as a followup, NOT a networking/production change): discovered + reproduced a pre-existing GUT test-suite-ordering hazard where tests/test_network_manager.gd's host()/disconnect_from_game() poisons the shared root MultiplayerAPI for every alphabetically-LATER test script that instantiates Player.tscn (is_server()/get_unique_id() start erroring after any real ENetMultiplayerPeer has been assigned-then-cleared once, even offline) -- this file was the first to be alphabetically affected (test_ability_system.gd was accidentally safe only by sorting before test_network_manager.gd); worked around it locally in this file's own before_all() (resets the SceneTree's MultiplayerAPI to a fresh instance) without touching NetworkManager.gd or any networking/production code (outside this agent's authority) -- filed TK-P2-26 (tools-devops) for the suite-wide proper fix. RE-SCOPE PROPOSAL for producer/architect sign-off: given the investigation confirmed most of the card's title was already satisfied by prior cards, and the net-new work here is genuinely small (1 new pure-rules file, ~2 small method additions, 1 signal, tests) -- recommend accepting this as the full closure of TK-P2-04's stated scope (role state machine + property swap; camera swap explicitly deferred to TK-P2-05 as already flagged) rather than requesting further expansion. Does NOT change any GDD rule, balance decision (Game_Balance.md's per-role speed values were already recorded/approved in Change Log [0.33]/[0.34] -- this card only WIRES them, does not decide them), or networking authority model. QA VERDICT: PASS-WITH-FOLLOWUP (qa-engineer, 2026-07-14). Regression re-run LOCALLY (Godot 4.7.stable headless, not trusting the reported number): `--headless --import` clean, then `-s addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd -gdir=res://tests -ginclude_subdirs -gexit` = 238/238 passed, 1378 asserts, 17 scripts, 5.4s -- matches the reported figure exactly; no S0/S1, no SCRIPT ERROR, no orphans/risky. test_role_state_machine.gd ran 16/16; its invalid-role case's push_error is the EXPECTED one (asserted via assert_push_error), and the [NET] WARNINGs are test_network_manager's intentional negative-path cases, not regressions. HUMAN-OBSERVABLE TEST DECISION: automation-only closure ACCEPTED for this card's scope. Rationale -- this card is local pure-logic wiring (role-value validation + a speed-profile lookup + a signal emit) with ZERO new RPC/network/host-authority surface (reviewer confirmed role is NOT on the MultiplayerSynchronizer/SceneReplicationConfig; assignment still flows through GameManager.apply_role_switch() from TK-P2-03, which was already human 2-instance verified 5/5 both directions). Correctness of that wiring IS fully covered here; only the subjective feel is deferred. title: สลับกล้อง First Person (เสือ) กับ Third Person (ผู้เล่นอื่น) ตามบทบาท
ทำ Safe Circle เป็นขอบเขตและ logic ที่เกี่ยวข้อง

title: Late-join / late-connect after Match Start: refuse or route peers that connect (or click Join) after the host has started the match
note: From TK-P2-13 code-review (round1 finding4) + qa. Two reachable states once Start fires: (a) a peer connecting during the spawn barrier window is deferred by PlayerSpawner (_deferred_join_peers) but NEVER spawned -> connected-but-Player-less; (b) a peer connecting after the host has left the WaitingRoom lands in a WaitingRoom whose host counterpart is freed (its _rpc_client_hello targets /root/WaitingRoom on a host that isn't there -> dead empty roster, can never start), and PlayerSpawner._on_peer_connected would spawn a driverless ghost avatar for everyone. Decide + implement: either REFUSE joins after Start (host rejects/closes the lobby on match start) or properly ROUTE late joiners into the running match (spawn them cleanly, put them in the arena). Server-authoritative. Not an S1 in the happy path (guarded), but a correctness/UX gap that must close before the Phase 2 Exit Gate.

title: Test-isolation: NetworkManager host()/disconnect_from_game() poisons the shared SceneTree MultiplayerAPI for alphabetically-later GUT scripts (is_server()/get_unique_id() break for any later Player.tscn authority test)
note: Discovered + reproduced (standalone repro script) while writing tests/test_role_state_machine.gd (TK-P2-04). GUT runs every tests/*.gd script in ONE shared process/SceneTree. tests/test_network_manager.gd's host()/join() tests assign a REAL ENetMultiplayerPeer to get_tree().get_multiplayer() -- the SAME root MultiplayerAPI every node in every OTHER test script also uses -- then clear it back to null on teardown. Empirically, Godot's SceneMultiplayer treats 'never had a peer' (is_server() conveniently defaults true, offline-friendly single-player default) and 'had a real peer, now cleared' (is_server() now correctly reports FALSE, get_unique_id() errors -- a real disconnected client should NOT still claim to be the server) as two DIFFERENT internal states, not the same 'offline' state. Once ANY test script assigns a real peer even once, EVERY test script that runs LATER in the same process and touches Player.tscn's is_multiplayer_authority()/get_unique_id() (CameraComponent._ready(), AbilityController._enter_tree(), etc.) inherits the 'disconnected' (not 'offline') state and fails with engine errors GUT treats as test failures. This is invisible in production (a real process only ever hosts/joins/stays offline once for its whole lifetime) and was invisible in this suite only because tests/test_ability_system.gd (the only pre-existing Player.tscn-instantiating test) happens to sort alphabetically BEFORE test_network_manager.gd -- not because it was actually safe; test_role_state_machine.gd sorts AFTER it and was the first to surface this. Worked around LOCALLY in test_role_state_machine.gd's own before_all() (resets the SceneTree's MultiplayerAPI to a fresh MultiplayerAPI.create_default_interface() instance) -- deliberately test-file-scoped, does NOT touch networking/NetworkManager.gd or any production/authority code (outside gameplay-engineer's authority per CLAUDE.md). Proper suite-wide fix belongs to whoever owns test infra/NetworkManager (tools-devops/network-engineer): either give test_network_manager.gd's peer-touching tests their OWN isolated MultiplayerAPI/root path (SceneTree.set_multiplayer(api, path)) instead of hijacking the shared root one, or add a GUT-level teardown hook that resets the root MultiplayerAPI after any test that assigns a real peer, so future test files don't depend on alphabetical-ordering luck the way test_ability_system.gd/test_role_state_machine.gd currently do.

title: Human feel-test: per-role MovementComponent speed profile (Outer 4.0/x1.5 vs Tiger 4.0/4.0-capped) once a Tiger is observable in a running session
note: Deferred human-observable pass carried forward from TK-P2-04's QA closure (PASS-WITH-FOLLOWUP) + code-review nit #1. TK-P2-04 wired Game_Balance.md §2's per-role speed profile into MovementComponent for the first time (Human/Outer walk 4.0 / sprint 6.0 = x1.5; Tiger walk AND sprint both capped at 4.0 = x1.0, no sprint advantage by design), plus shifted the shared baseline from the old flat 5.0 / x1.4 to the role-based values for EVERY player. All of this is CORRECTNESS-verified by automation (GUT 238/238, pure + Player.tscn integration cases) and has ZERO network/host-authority surface, so TK-P2-04 closed on automation alone. What automation CANNOT cover is the subjective FEEL: (a) does the Tiger's no-sprint-advantage cap read as 'stalk, not chase' in a live round; (b) does the Outer 4.0/6.0 baseline shift feel right vs the old flat 5.0/x1.4; (c) does the profile actually swap on the human who becomes the new Tiger mid-round. This is NOT observable today -- no Tiger exists in a running session until TK-P2-09 (first-Tiger) lands, TK-P2-05 (FP/TP camera) is still todo, and the TK-P2-03 F7 force-Tiger debug hook was removed post-close, so there is currently no manual role-swap trigger. ACTION: once TK-P2-09 (and ideally TK-P2-05 so the view swap is visible too) is in, fold this into that human N-window pass rather than running a standalone session -- verify Tiger vs Outer walk/sprint feel live, the swap applies to the correct human on tag, and the profile reverts on the ex-Tiger. Also (optional, from review nit #4) add a Tiger-starting-state invalid-role rejection case to tests/test_role_state_machine.gd while touching the file (guard is a symmetric early-return so risk is low). NOT a bug and NOT blocking any gate -- a deferred feel-verification for RTM traceability.
